entries.status: No EU-level schedule or class. EU legislation does not establish classes of narcotic or psychotropic substances; Member States classify drugs according to the 1961, 1971 and 1988 UN Conventions. The Framework Decision on illicit drug trafficking defines 'drug' as any substance covered by the 1961 Single Convention (as amended by the 1972 Protocol) or by the 1971 Convention, or listed in its Annex.

entries.note: Both targeted look-ups found the excluded position (position removed from 1 January 2013) and both full readings the lysergic acid entry. The list does not say that lysergide is a derivative of lysergic acid. Note 6 of the Perechen defines derivatives as substances not listed on their own (in the Perechen or the State Register of Medicines) whose structure is formed by «заменой (формальным замещением) одного или нескольких атомов водорода, галогенов и (или) гидроксильных групп» with other atoms or substituents (not hydroxyl or carboxyl groups), the substituents together having no more carbon atoms than the parent; if several parents fit, the one needing the fewest substituents decides.
